metadata.case_name: KWOK SUI SHUM DOROTHY v. HUI LAM HO AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: Accounting work for Tupperware Asia Pacific (a division of Premiere Products Incorporated)
plaintiff.occupation_after: Insurance agent; assisting at Bishi Mizuiki with accounts and other work

injuries.description: Madam Kwok sustained a soft tissue injury (often termed "whiplash") to her neck at the time of her traffic accident in May 1998
source: "Madam Kwok sustained a soft tissue injury (often termed "whiplash") to her neck at the time of her traffic accident in May 1998"
injuries.icd_description: Acute whiplash associated disorder with complaint of neck pain, stiffness or tenderness only

injuries.description: Cervical spondylosis / degenerative disease of the cervical spine
source: "MRI ... revealed degenerative disease of the cervical spine and prolapse of disc at C3/4 and C5/6 levels."

injuries.description: Prolapse of disc at C3/4 and C5/6 levels (MRI)
source: "revealed degenerative disease of the cervical spine and prolapse of disc at C3/4 and C5/6 levels."

"The prolapse of disc at C5/6 level caused narrowing the left lateral recess and left neuroforamen, which was compatible with the clinical finding of left upper limb neurological disturbance caused by the traffic accident."
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the neck

manifestations.description: Periodical neck pain with each episode lasting for 3 to 5 days
Fleeting paraesthesiae in the left upper extremity; occasional left forearm and left thumb numbness

treatments_received: Attended Accident and Emergency (Queen Mary Hospital) and left without consultation
Consulted bonesetter on the day after the accident (and on several subsequent occasions)
Seen by Dr Michael Lee (Canossa Hospital)
Psychiatric treatment (Dr Leo Chiu, Dr Chan Chung Man and Dr Chung See Yuen; outpatient psychiatric clinic of Pamela Youde Nethersole Eastern Hospital)
treatments_future: Psychiatric counselling (assessment: needs treatment for two more years; frequency around once a month)
Possible anterior spinal fusion of the cervical spine (surgery)

losses.description: Pain, suffering and loss of amenities arising from neck injury (whiplash) and associated psychiatric impairment
Panic attack / hyperventilation / panic disorder Anxiety and depressive problems (mild)
